Shared0.description: Provenance metadata for this asset, overrides manifest-level provenance

ai_tool.description: AI system used to generate or modify this content. Aligns with IPTC 2025.1 AI metadata fields and C2PA claim_generator.

name.description: Name of the AI tool or model (e.g., 'DALL-E 3', 'Stable Diffusion XL', 'Gemini')

provider.description: Organization that provides the AI tool (e.g., 'OpenAI', 'Stability AI', 'Google')

version.description: Version identifier for the AI tool or model (e.g., '25.1', '0125', '2.1'). For generative models, use the model version rather than the API version.

c2pa.description: C2PA sidecar manifest reference. Links to a detached cryptographic provenance manifest for this content. Note: file-level C2PA bindings break when ad servers transcode, resize, or re-encode assets. For pipelines with intermediaries, consider embedded_provenance as the primary provenance mechanism.

manifest_url.description: URL to the C2PA manifest store for this content

created_time.description: When this content was created or generated (ISO 8601)

declared_at.description: When this provenance claim was made (ISO 8601). Distinct from created_time, which records when the content itself was produced. A provenance claim may be attached well after content creation, for example when retroactively declaring AI involvement for regulatory compliance.

declared_by.description: Party declaring this provenance. Identifies who attached the provenance claim, enabling receiving parties to assess trust.

agent_url.description: URL of the agent or service that declared this provenance

role.description: Role of the declaring party in the supply chain

enumDescriptions.advertiser: The brand or advertiser that owns the content
enumDescriptions.agency: Agency acting on behalf of the advertiser
enumDescriptions.creator: The party that created or generated the content
enumDescriptions.platform: Ad platform or publisher that processed the content
enumDescriptions.tool: Automated tool or service that attached provenance metadata

digital_source_type.description: IPTC-aligned classification of AI involvement in producing this content

enumDescriptions.algorithmic_media: Produced by deterministic algorithms without machine learning (procedural generation, rule-based systems)
enumDescriptions.composite_capture: Multiple digital captures composited together without AI
enumDescriptions.composite_synthetic: Composite of multiple elements where at least one is AI-generated (e.g., stock photo composited with AI-generated background)
enumDescriptions.composite_with_trained_algorithmic_media: Human-created content combined with AI-generated elements (e.g., photo with AI background)
enumDescriptions.data_driven_media: Assembled from structured data feeds (DCO templates, product catalogs, weather-triggered variants)
enumDescriptions.digital_capture: Captured by a digital device (camera, scanner, screen recording) with no AI involvement
enumDescriptions.digital_creation: Created by a human using digital tools (Photoshop, Illustrator, After Effects) without AI generation
enumDescriptions.human_edits: Content augmented, corrected, or enhanced by humans using non-generative tools
enumDescriptions.trained_algorithmic_media: Generated entirely by a trained AI model (DALL-E, Midjourney, Stable Diffusion, Sora)

digital_source_type.title: Digital Source Type

disclosure.description: Regulatory disclosure requirements for this content. Indicates whether AI disclosure is required and under which jurisdictions.

label_text.description: Required disclosure label text for this jurisdiction, in the local language

region.description: Sub-national region code (e.g., 'CA' for California, 'BY' for Bavaria)

render_guidance.description: How the disclosure should be rendered for this jurisdiction. Expresses the declaring party's intent for persistence and position based on regulatory requirements. Publishers control actual rendering but governance agents can audit whether guidance was followed.

min_duration_ms.description: Minimum display duration in milliseconds for initial persistence. Recommended when persistence is initial — without it, the duration is at the publisher's discretion. At serve time the publisher reads this from provenance since the brief is not available.

persistence.description: How long the disclosure must persist during content playback or display

enumDescriptions.continuous: Disclosure must remain visible or audible throughout the entire content display duration. For video and audio, this means the full playback duration. For static formats (display, DOOH), this means the full display slot. For DOOH specifically, 'content duration' means the ad's display slot within the rotation, not the screen's full rotation cycle.
enumDescriptions.flexible: Disclosure presence is sufficient; placement timing and duration are at the publisher's discretion
enumDescriptions.initial: Disclosure must appear at the start of content for a minimum duration before it may be removed. Pair with min_duration_ms in render_guidance or creative brief to specify the required duration.

persistence.title: Disclosure Persistence

positions.description: Preferred disclosure positions in priority order. The first position a format supports should be used.

items.description: Where a required disclosure should appear within a creative. Used by creative briefs to specify disclosure placement and by formats to declare which positions they can render.
items.title: Disclosure Position

required.description: The declaring party's claim that AI disclosure is required for this content under applicable regulations. This is a declared signal carried through the supply chain — useful as a routing and audit input — not a regulatory determination made by the protocol. Receiving parties remain responsible for their own jurisdictional analysis and should not treat `required: false` as compliance cover.

embedded_provenance.description: Provenance metadata embedded within the content stream. Each entry declares one embedding layer: structured provenance data carried inside the content itself, as distinct from sidecar references (c2pa.manifest_url). Embedded provenance survives operations that break sidecar and file-level bindings: ad-server transcoding, CMS ingestion, copy-paste, reformatting, and CDN re-encoding. For ad-tech pipelines where content passes through multiple intermediaries, embedded provenance is the reliable path for provenance that persists from declaration through delivery. This is a declaration by the embedding party. The receiving party (the seller) is the verifier-of-record: it confirms the claim by calling a governance agent it trusts (typically one published in `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers`).

embedded_at.description: When the provenance data was embedded (ISO 8601)

method.description: How provenance data is carried within the content

enumDescriptions.manifest_wrapper: A provenance manifest embedded in the file container per format-specific rules (e.g., JUMBF box in JPEG, C2PATextManifestWrapper in plaintext per C2PA Section A.7). The manifest travels with the file but is tied to the file's byte structure.
enumDescriptions.provenance_markers: Invisible markers embedded within the content stream that encode or reference a provenance record. Designed to survive reformatting, copy-paste, CMS ingestion, and ad-server transcoding that breaks file-level bindings.

method.title: Embedded Provenance Method

provider.description: Organization that performed the embedding (e.g., 'Encypher', 'Digimarc'). Display label and audit context — not a wire identifier.

standard.description: Standard the embedding conforms to, if any (e.g., 'c2pa' for C2PA Section A.7 text manifest embedding)

verify_agent.description: Buyer's representation that this embedding can be verified by a governance agent on the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers` list. The `agent_url` MUST match (canonicalized) one of the seller's published `accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` entries; sellers reject `sync_creatives` submissions whose `verify_agent.agent_url` is off-list with `PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_NOT_ACCEPTED`. This is buyer-supplied evidence, not buyer-driven routing — the seller is the verifier-of-record and the seller controls which agent it actually calls (the seller MAY use a different on-list agent if it determines this is more appropriate; the seller does not call buyer-asserted endpoints outside its allowlist). MAY be omitted for self-verifiable embeddings (e.g., a C2PA text manifest with a public key the seller already trusts).

agent_url.description: URL of the governance agent the buyer represents was used to embed/verify this layer. MUST use the `https://` scheme and MUST appear in the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` list (canonicalized per /docs/reference/url-canonicalization: lowercase scheme and host, strip default port, normalize path dot-segments). Sellers MUST NOT call this URL until the canonicalized match is confirmed.
agent_url.title: HTTPS URL

feature_id.description: Optional `feature_id` the buyer represents the seller should request via `get_creative_features` (e.g., `encypher.markers_present_v2`). SHOULD match the `feature_id` declared on the matching `accepted_verifiers[]` entry, or be omitted to defer the selector to the seller. When the seller's entry pins a `feature_id`, that value wins; when neither side pins, the seller selects from the agent's `governance.creative_features` catalog.

human_oversight.description: Level of human involvement in the AI-assisted creation process. Independent of `disclosure.required` — the protocol does not derive disclosure obligations from oversight level. Some regulations include carve-outs for human-edited or human-directed AI output, but those carve-outs have factual prerequisites the schema cannot evaluate. Asserting `edited` or `directed` does not by itself justify `disclosure.required: false`.

enumDescriptions.directed: Human directed the creative process with AI as an assistive tool
enumDescriptions.edited: Human edited or refined AI-generated output
enumDescriptions.none: Fully automated with no human involvement in generation
enumDescriptions.prompt_only: Human provided the prompt or instructions but did not review outputs
enumDescriptions.selected: Human selected from multiple AI-generated candidates

synthetic_depiction.description: Assessed declaration of whether the content synthetically depicts a real or fictional person performing or appearing in a way that was generated or materially manipulated rather than captured as depicted. `true` covers both a fully synthetic performer and material manipulation of a real performer; `false` is an assessed declaration that the content does not contain such a depiction. Absence means the content has not been assessed for synthetic depiction. This field does not claim consent, legality, or independent verification, and receivers MUST NOT derive it solely from `digital_source_type`.

verification.description: Third-party verification or detection results for this content. Multiple services may independently evaluate the same content. Provenance is a claim — verification results attached by the declaring party are supplementary. The enforcing party (e.g., seller/publisher) should run its own verification via get_creative_features or calibrate_content.

confidence.description: Confidence score of the verification result (0.0 to 1.0)

details_url.description: URL to the full verification report

verified_by.description: Name of the verification service (e.g., 'DoubleVerify', 'Hive Moderation', 'Reality Defender')

watermarks.description: Content watermarks applied to this asset. Each entry declares one watermarking layer: a content modification that encodes an identifier or fingerprint within the asset. Watermarks differ from embedded provenance: a watermark encodes an identifier (who generated it, who owns it), while embedded provenance carries or references a structured provenance record (the full chain of custody). A single asset may carry both. Aligns with C2PA action taxonomy: c2pa.watermarked.bound (watermark linked to a C2PA manifest) and c2pa.watermarked.unbound (watermark independent of any manifest). This is a declaration by the watermarking party. The receiving party (the seller) is the verifier-of-record: it confirms the claim by calling a governance agent it trusts (typically one published in `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers`).

c2pa_action.description: C2PA action classification for this watermark

enumDescriptions.c2pa.watermarked.bound: Watermark linked to a C2PA manifest for this asset. The watermark and manifest are mutually reinforcing: the manifest references the watermark, and the watermark can be used to locate the manifest.
enumDescriptions.c2pa.watermarked.unbound: Watermark independent of any C2PA manifest. Applied before any provenance signing event (e.g., by the AI generator at creation time) or in pipelines where no manifest is present.

c2pa_action.title: C2PA Watermark Action

media_type.description: Media category of the watermarked content

enumDescriptions.audio: Watermark applied to audio content (e.g., spread-spectrum, echo hiding)
enumDescriptions.image: Watermark applied to image content (e.g., spatial domain, frequency domain)
enumDescriptions.text: Watermark applied to text content (e.g., synonym substitution, structural modification)
enumDescriptions.video: Watermark applied to video content (e.g., per-frame image watermarking, temporal watermarking)

media_type.title: Watermark Media Type

provider.description: Organization that applied the watermark (e.g., 'Imatag', 'Steg.AI', 'Encypher'). Display label and audit context — not a wire identifier.

verify_agent.description: Buyer's representation that this watermark can be detected by a governance agent on the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers` list. The `agent_url` MUST match (canonicalized) one of the seller's published `accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` entries; sellers reject `sync_creatives` submissions whose `verify_agent.agent_url` is off-list with `PROVENANCE_VERIFIER_NOT_ACCEPTED`. This is buyer-supplied evidence, not buyer-driven routing — the seller is the verifier-of-record and the seller controls which agent it actually calls (the seller MAY use a different on-list agent if it determines this is more appropriate; the seller does not call buyer-asserted endpoints outside its allowlist).

agent_url.description: URL of the governance agent the buyer represents was used to apply/detect this watermark. MUST use the `https://` scheme and MUST appear in the seller's `creative_policy.accepted_verifiers[].agent_url` list (canonicalized per /docs/reference/url-canonicalization: lowercase scheme and host, strip default port, normalize path dot-segments). Sellers MUST NOT call this URL until the canonicalized match is confirmed.
agent_url.title: HTTPS URL

feature_id.description: Optional `feature_id` the buyer represents the seller should request via `get_creative_features` (e.g., `imatag.watermark_detected`). SHOULD match the `feature_id` declared on the matching `accepted_verifiers[]` entry, or be omitted to defer the selector to the seller. When the seller's entry pins a `feature_id`, that value wins; when neither side pins, the seller selects from the agent's `governance.creative_features` catalog.

Shared1.description: Extension object for platform-specific, vendor-namespaced parameters. Extensions are always optional and must be namespaced under a vendor/platform key (e.g., ext.gam, ext.roku). Used for custom capabilities, partner-specific configuration, and features being proposed for standardization.
Shared1.title: Extension Object

Shared2.description: Governed family for a creative macro token. `vendor` is qualified by an authority-controlled namespace and immutable revision on the declaration/capability; AdCP does not enumerate companies as dialects. `unknown` is declaration-only and always byte-preserved.

enumDescriptions.adcp: AdCP universal macro syntax and semantics.
enumDescriptions.iab_daast: IAB DAAST macro syntax, qualified by the referenced specification/registry revision.
enumDescriptions.iab_vast: IAB VAST macro syntax, qualified by the referenced live-registry revision.
enumDescriptions.unknown: The token namespace cannot be established. Preserve the token unchanged and never advertise it as resolvable.
enumDescriptions.vendor: A vendor- or platform-owned macro namespace, qualified by its authoritative URI and immutable revision.

Shared2.title: Macro Dialect Family

Shared3.description: Evidence level connecting a dialect-local macro meaning to the AdCP universal vocabulary.

enumDescriptions.dialect_defined: The dialect defines the token, but no AdCP universal semantic is asserted.
enumDescriptions.unresolved: No safe meaning is established; the token remains byte-preserved.
enumDescriptions.verified_universal: The cited dialect mapping verifies an AdCP universal semantic.

Shared9.description: Standardized macro placeholders for dynamic value substitution in creative tracking URLs. Macros are replaced with actual values at impression time. See docs/creative/universal-macros.mdx for detailed documentation.

enumDescriptions.APP_ITEM_ID: Mobile app identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.AXEM: AXE contextual metadata (encoded blob). Legacy — in TMP, use Offer creative_data for dynamic creative values and TMPX for exposure tracking.
enumDescriptions.CATALOG_ID: Buyer-defined catalog identifier from the catalog's catalog_id field
enumDescriptions.CLICK_URL: Publisher's click tracking URL (auto-inserted by sales agent)
enumDescriptions.CREATIVE_VARIANT_ID: Seller-assigned creative variant identifier, passed through at serve time
enumDescriptions.DESTINATION_ID: Travel destination identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.DEVICE_TYPE: Device category (mobile, tablet, desktop, ctv, dooh)
enumDescriptions.FLIGHT_ID: Flight route identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.GPP_SID: GPP Section ID(s) indicating applicable privacy framework sections
enumDescriptions.GTIN: Global Trade Item Number for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.HOTEL_ID: Hotel property identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.IMPRESSION_ID: Opaque, collision-resistant identifier for one impression opportunity. Used for impression deduplication, cross-vendor reconciliation, pixel-retry dedup, and TMP cross-identity exposure dedup. Minted by the publisher, ad-decision layer, or buyer at {TMPX} decode; required upstream for TMP context-only impressions where {TMPX} is absent.
enumDescriptions.INSTALLMENT_ID: Installment identifier (podcast episode, print issue, etc.)
enumDescriptions.IP_ADDRESS: User IP address (often masked for privacy, may return empty)
enumDescriptions.ITEM_DESCRIPTION: Description of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: description). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_NAME: Name/title of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: name). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE: Price amount of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.amount). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE_CURRENCY: ISO 4217 currency code of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.currency). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_TAGLINE: Short promotional tagline of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: tagline). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.JOB_ID: Job posting identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.LISTING_ID: Real estate listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OFFERING_ID: AdCP offering identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OS: Operating system (iOS, Android, tvOS, Roku, etc.)
enumDescriptions.POD_SIZE: Total ads in the ad break
enumDescriptions.PROGRAM_ID: Education program identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.SKU: Product SKU identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.STORE_ID: Store location identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.TMPX: TMP exposure token — HPKE-encrypted identity tokens for per-user exposure tracking. Produced by Identity Match, substituted into creative tracking URLs, received by the buyer's impression pixel.
enumDescriptions.VEHICLE_ID: Vehicle listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered

description: Typed seller collateral for buyer-facing product cards. Each entry carries a semantic role (coverage_map, sample_render, etc.) and a canonical asset payload. Distinct from hero_image/carousel_images (display-oriented) and from core/reference-asset.json (creative-generation oriented).

asset.description: The asset payload, discriminated on asset_type (image, video, markdown, url).

oneOf.description: Image asset with URL and dimensions

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as an image asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

breakpoint_id.description: Binding used only when this image populates a `seller_rendered_stateful_display` `state_canvases` slot. It MUST match one breakpoint declared on the selected state (semantic validators resolve it). Omit for ordinary image slots.

file_size_bytes.description: Image file size in bytes. Required by agents that advertise a max_file_size_kb constraint.

focal_point.description: Normalized `[x, y]` coordinates (0–1 from top-left) of the image's visual anchor. Seller-side renderers crop toward the focal point when deriving renditions across breakpoints and aspect ratios; absent, cropping falls back to center-weighted defaults.

format.description: Image file format (jpg, png, gif, webp, etc.)

pixel_ratio.description: Intrinsic pixels per logical render pixel (for example `2` for a 600×500 image intended to render at 300×250). Optional because a validator can infer the ratio when the target format declares logical dimensions. When supplied, it MUST agree with both `width / logical_width` and `height / logical_height`; it is never a substitute for the intrinsic `width` and `height` fields.

state_id.description: Binding used only when this image populates a `seller_rendered_stateful_display` `state_canvases` slot. It MUST match one declared `states[].state_id` (semantic validators resolve it). Omit for ordinary image slots.

oneOf.$comment: Dimension policy is deliberate and differs by asset type: a hosted `video` asset requires width/height (intrinsic pixels of a concrete file), while the `vast` asset omits them entirely (renditions are selected per-MediaFile by the player at serve time). Do not infer that AdCP forces a single width/height onto all video — only onto hosted files.
oneOf.description: A hosted video file delivered directly (e.g., an MP4 you host), with URL and technical specifications including audio track properties. `width` and `height` are required because a hosted video file has intrinsic, native pixel dimensions that are known when the file is created. Tag-delivered video uses the separate `vast` asset, which carries no `width`/`height`: a VAST response resolves geometry per-`MediaFile` at serve time, so there is no single width/height for the ad. Aspect-ratio and size *constraints* (what a placement accepts) belong on the format/requirements layer, not on the asset.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a video asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

audio_bitrate_kbps.description: Audio bitrate in kilobits per second

audio_codec.description: Audio codec used (aac, aac_lc, he_aac, pcm, mp3, ac3, eac3, etc.)

audio_description_url.description: URL to audio description track for visually impaired users

captions_url.description: URL to captions file (WebVTT, SRT, etc.)

container_format.description: Video container format (mp4, webm, mov, etc.)

frame_rate.description: Frame rate as string to preserve precision (e.g., '23.976', '29.97', '30')

frame_rate_type.description: Whether the video uses a constant or variable frame rate. Broadcast and SSAI contexts require constant frame rate for seamless splicing.

enumDescriptions.constant: Constant frame rate (CFR) — each frame occupies an identical time interval
enumDescriptions.variable: Variable frame rate (VFR) — frame intervals may differ

frame_rate_type.title: Frame Rate Type

gop_type.description: Group of Pictures structure. SSAI and broadcast require closed GOPs for clean splice points; open GOPs may produce artifacts at ad boundaries.

enumDescriptions.closed: Each GOP is independently decodable — required for SSAI and broadcast splicing
enumDescriptions.open: GOPs may reference frames from adjacent GOPs — not suitable for splicing

gop_type.title: GOP Type

has_audio.description: Whether the video contains an audio track

hdr_format.description: HDR format if applicable, or 'sdr' for standard dynamic range

height.description: Height in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native height. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no height; see the `vast` asset.)

moov_atom_position.description: Position of the moov atom in an MP4 container. 'start' enables progressive download without buffering the entire file; required for streaming ad delivery.

enumDescriptions.end: moov atom at end of file — requires full download before playback can begin
enumDescriptions.start: moov atom at beginning of file — enables progressive download and streaming delivery

moov_atom_position.title: Moov Atom Position

scan_type.description: Video scan method. Modern digital delivery requires progressive scan; interlaced is retained for broadcast legacy content.

enumDescriptions.interlaced: Alternating lines drawn in two passes per frame (legacy broadcast)
enumDescriptions.progressive: All lines of each frame are drawn in sequence

scan_type.title: Scan Type

transcript_url.description: URL to text transcript of the video content

video_bitrate_kbps.description: Video stream bitrate in kilobits per second

video_codec.description: Video codec used (h264, h265, vp9, av1, prores, etc.)

width.description: Width in pixels — the video file's intrinsic native width. Required: a hosted file always has concrete dimensions. (Tag-delivered video carries no width; see the `vast` asset.)

allow_raw_html.description: Whether raw HTML blocks are allowed in the markdown. False recommended for security.

oneOf.$comment: Fallback table is also rendered in docs/creative/asset-types.mdx (URL Asset section). Keep the two in sync — schema description is the normative source for conformance tools; mdx is the human-readable copy.
oneOf.description: URL reference asset. `url_type` declares the mechanism a receiver uses to invoke the URL (`clickthrough`, display `ad_request`, `tracker_pixel`, or `tracker_script`) and is distinct from the URL's purpose, which the format declares in `url-asset-requirements.role`. Senders SHOULD include `url_type` on every URL asset. When `url_type` is absent, receivers SHOULD fall back to the format's role: clickthrough/landing_page → `clickthrough`; impression_tracker/click_tracker → `tracker_pixel`; viewability_tracker → `tracker_script`; third_party_tracker and display ad requests have no safe fallback. When neither `url_type` nor a format-side role is available, receivers MUST NOT silently pick a mechanism. VAST/DAAST tag URLs are not URL assets — use `asset_type: "vast"` or `asset_type: "daast"`.

asset_type.description: Discriminator identifying this as a URL asset. See /schemas/creative/asset-types for the registry.

description.description: Description of what this URL points to

macro_declarations.description: One declaration per token occurrence in `url`; declaration_id values MUST be unique and every location MUST identify an existing occurrence. Absence retains legacy opaque transport behavior.

allOf.description: The source-faithful contract for one occurrence of one macro token. It identifies the current dialect, verified mapping status, exact asset-field occurrence, next processing operation, actor, and encoding. Translation and concrete value resolution are separate operations: a translator emits the declared native token and replaces this declaration with the target declaration. Unknown tokens are always byte-preserved.

declaration_id.description: Identifier unique within the enclosing asset, used to correlate validation results.

dialect_namespace.description: Authority-controlled registry or mapping URI. Required for IAB VAST, IAB DAAST, and vendor dialects.

dialect_revision.description: Immutable registry/mapping revision, release, commit, or digest. Required for IAB VAST, IAB DAAST, and vendor dialects.

dialect_semantic.description: Exact semantic identifier in the cited dialect, such as `CACHEBUSTING`, `PLAYERSTATE`, or a documented vendor name. This is not inferred from token spelling.

encoding.description: Encoding for the concrete value. Translation/preservation uses `none` at depth zero.
encoding.title: Macro Encoding

context.description: Syntactic occurrence context supported by the first macro contract. Substitution inside arbitrary JavaScript, JSON, or HTML text is intentionally not inferred; use `opaque` and preserve it unless a later governed context is added.
context.title: Macro Value Context

occurrence.description: Zero-based occurrence of this exact token within the named field.

operation.description: The next authorized operation on the current source token.

enumDescriptions.preserve: Leave the source bytes unchanged because no safe local operation is established.
enumDescriptions.resolve_value: Insert the concrete runtime value using the declared encoding contract.
enumDescriptions.translate_to_native: Replace the current token with a declared downstream-native token; no concrete runtime value is inserted at this step.

operation.title: Macro Processing Operation

performed_by.description: Actor authorized to perform the declared translation or value resolution. Omitted for preservation.

enumDescriptions.buyer: The buyer agent acts before submission.
enumDescriptions.creative_agent: The creative agent executing build_creative, preview_creative, or validate_input performs the declared build-time operation.
enumDescriptions.request_executor: The component executing the governed request acts, whether a client player, publisher player, SSAI service, or another request executor.
enumDescriptions.seller: The AdCP seller or its execution adapter acts during trafficking or serving.
enumDescriptions.source_ad_server: The originating creative/ad server acts on its own native token.

performed_by.title: Macro Processing Actor

required.description: Whether terminal delivery must fail if the declared operation cannot complete.

token.description: Exact byte-preserved token expression at this occurrence, including delimiters.

translation_target.description: Required only for `translate_to_native`. The output token contract that replaces this declaration after translation.

encoding.description: Exact encoding profile applied to a concrete substitution value. `rfc3986` encodes UTF-8 bytes outside the RFC 3986 unreserved set once per depth. `iab_vast_uri` follows the cited IAB VAST macro registry, including its array serialization rules, and is exactly one pass.
encoding.title: Macro Encoding

performed_by.description: Protocol role authorized to translate the token or bind its concrete value.

enumDescriptions.buyer: The buyer agent acts before submission.
enumDescriptions.creative_agent: The creative agent executing build_creative, preview_creative, or validate_input performs the declared build-time operation.
enumDescriptions.request_executor: The component executing the governed request acts, whether a client player, publisher player, SSAI service, or another request executor.
enumDescriptions.seller: The AdCP seller or its execution adapter acts during trafficking or serving.
enumDescriptions.source_ad_server: The originating creative/ad server acts on its own native token.

performed_by.title: Macro Processing Actor

translation_target.title: Macro Translation Target

unavailable_behavior.description: Action when the responsible actor has no value. Omission is legal only for a complete URL query-value occurrence; dialect sentinels require a cited dialect rule.

universal_semantic.description: Verified AdCP universal meaning. Present only when mapping_status is `verified_universal`.

enumDescriptions.APP_ITEM_ID: Mobile app identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.AXEM: AXE contextual metadata (encoded blob). Legacy — in TMP, use Offer creative_data for dynamic creative values and TMPX for exposure tracking.
enumDescriptions.CATALOG_ID: Buyer-defined catalog identifier from the catalog's catalog_id field
enumDescriptions.CLICK_URL: Publisher's click tracking URL (auto-inserted by sales agent)
enumDescriptions.CREATIVE_VARIANT_ID: Seller-assigned creative variant identifier, passed through at serve time
enumDescriptions.DESTINATION_ID: Travel destination identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.DEVICE_TYPE: Device category (mobile, tablet, desktop, ctv, dooh)
enumDescriptions.FLIGHT_ID: Flight route identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.GPP_SID: GPP Section ID(s) indicating applicable privacy framework sections
enumDescriptions.GTIN: Global Trade Item Number for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.HOTEL_ID: Hotel property identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.IMPRESSION_ID: Opaque, collision-resistant identifier for one impression opportunity. Used for impression deduplication, cross-vendor reconciliation, pixel-retry dedup, and TMP cross-identity exposure dedup. Minted by the publisher, ad-decision layer, or buyer at {TMPX} decode; required upstream for TMP context-only impressions where {TMPX} is absent.
enumDescriptions.INSTALLMENT_ID: Installment identifier (podcast episode, print issue, etc.)
enumDescriptions.IP_ADDRESS: User IP address (often masked for privacy, may return empty)
enumDescriptions.ITEM_DESCRIPTION: Description of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: description). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_NAME: Name/title of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: name). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE: Price amount of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.amount). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_PRICE_CURRENCY: ISO 4217 currency code of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: price.currency). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.ITEM_TAGLINE: Short promotional tagline of the catalog item being rendered (catalog_field: tagline). Catalog content macro — scalar text value substituted under the catalog-item substitution-safety rules.
enumDescriptions.JOB_ID: Job posting identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.LISTING_ID: Real estate listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OFFERING_ID: AdCP offering identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.OS: Operating system (iOS, Android, tvOS, Roku, etc.)
enumDescriptions.POD_SIZE: Total ads in the ad break
enumDescriptions.PROGRAM_ID: Education program identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.SKU: Product SKU identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.STORE_ID: Store location identifier for the catalog item being rendered
enumDescriptions.TMPX: TMP exposure token — HPKE-encrypted identity tokens for per-user exposure tracking. Produced by Identity Match, substituted into creative tracking URLs, received by the buyer's impression pixel.
enumDescriptions.VEHICLE_ID: Vehicle listing identifier for the catalog item being rendered

universal_semantic.title: Universal Macro

verifier_constraints.adcp_semantic_identity: when dialect is adcp, dialect_semantic must equal universal_semantic
verifier_constraints.asset_field: location.field must exist on and be permitted by the containing asset type
verifier_constraints.catalog_universal_profile: catalog semantics require seller resolve_value in a URL context with exactly one rfc3986 pass
verifier_constraints.declaration_id_uniqueness: declaration_id must be unique within the containing asset
verifier_constraints.omit_parameter_scope: omit_parameter requires the token to occupy the complete URL query-parameter value
verifier_constraints.token_occurrence: location must identify the declared zero-based occurrence of token in location.field

state_id.description: Binding used only when this URL populates a `seller_rendered_stateful_display` `state_click_urls` slot. It MUST match one declared `states[].state_id` (semantic validators resolve it); at most one entry per state. Omit for ordinary URL slots.

url.description: URL reference carrying plain, AdCP, IAB, or declared vendor macro syntax. Buyers preserve token delimiters; the authoritative declaration determines the processing operation and encoding.
url.title: Macro-bearing URL

verifier_constraints.macro_aware_uri: mask recognized token lexical forms with an RFC3986 unreserved sentinel, whether declared or on the undeclared 3.x compatibility path, then require a valid absolute HTTP or HTTPS URI; masking assigns no semantics

url_type.description: Mechanism a receiver uses to invoke this URL: `clickthrough` for a user destination, `ad_request` for a third-party display creative request, `tracker_pixel` for an event HTTP request, or `tracker_script` for a script include. SHOULD be present on every URL asset.
url_type.title: URL Asset Type

oneOf.title: URL Asset

description.description: Optional human-readable context about this asset.

role.description: Semantic role of this asset. coverage_map: geographic or audience reach visualization; sample_render: mockup of ad placement in context; environment_photo: photo of the physical or digital environment; media_kit: downloadable media kit or spec sheet; logo: seller or property logo; other: seller-defined role (provide role_label).

role_label.description: Human-readable label for the asset role. Required when role is 'other'; optional otherwise.
